newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says March-May industry output up 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: EU says March-May industry output up 1.1 pct.

text.p: Industrial production grew 1.1 percent in the European Union in the period March to May compared with the previous three months, Eurostat said on Tuesday.
"This confirms the upswing seen in the previous few months," the EU's statistics office said in a statement.
Among the 10 member states included in the statistics, nine showed higher output figures. Only Britain saw a decline, down by 0.2 percent in the three-month period.
Spain and Italy recorded the fastest rise in output growth, of 2.0 and 1.6 percent respectively.
Output in the motor vehicle manufacturing industry rose by 3.0 percent, the largest increase among individual industries.
However, growth in the EU was still slightly below the pace in both the United States and in Japan, up by 1.3 and 1.2 percent.
Compared with the same month last year, EU industry output rose by 2.5 percent in May. Finland showed the biggest increase, up by 5.2 percent, while Britain again had a decline, down by 1.8 percent.
Eurostat's figures measure production volume of the total industry, excluding construction, adjusted for seasonal and one-off fluctuations.
